pyramid_texts.title: Sarcophagus Chamber South Wall — Unas Enthroned with Osiris
pyramid_texts.t:
§134: O Unas, you have not gone dead, you have gone alive to sit on the throne of Osiris. Your scepter is in your hand that you may give orders to the living, the handle of your lotus-shaped scepter in your hand. Give orders to those of the Mysterious Sites, the dead!

§135: Your arm is that of Atum, your shoulders are those of Atum, your belly is that of Atum, your back is that of Atum, your bottom is that of Atum, your two legs are those of Atum, your face is that of Anubis. The sites of Horus serve you, the sites of Seth serve you.

pyramid_texts.title: Sarcophagus Chamber South Wall — Beware of the Lake; Ascent to Re
pyramid_texts.t:
§136: O Unas, beware of the Lake!
To say four times: The messengers of your Ka have come to you, the messengers of your father have come to you, the messengers of Re have come to you.

§137: Go after your sun! You are to purify yourself. Your bones are those of female hawks, the goddesses who are in heaven, so that you may be by the side of the god and leave your house to your son, your procreation. Everyone who shall speak evil against the name of Unas,

§138: when you go up, is predestined by Geb to be a despised one of his city, so that he shall flee and falter. You are to purify yourself with the cool water of the stars, and you will climb down upon ropes of brass — on the arms of Horus, in his name He-of-the-Henu-Barge.

§139: The glorified humanity bewail you after the Imperishable Stars have carried you. Enter, then, into the place where your father is, where Geb is! He gives you that which was on the brow of Horus, so that you become powerful and full of glory through it, so that you become the one at the head of the Westerners through it.

pyramid_texts.title: Sarcophagus Chamber South Wall — Horus, Seth, and the Imperishable Stars
pyramid_texts.t:
§140: O Unas! Your messengers go, your heralds hurry to your father, to Atum. "Atum, let him rise to you, fold him in your arms!

§141: There is no god, who has become a star, without a companion." "Shall I be your companion?" "Look at me! you have seen the forms of the children of their fathers, who know their spell, who are now Imperishable Stars." May you see the two inhabitants of the Palace — this is Horus and Seth!

§142: May you bespit the face of Horus and remove his injury! May you catch the testicles of Seth and remove his mutilation! That one is born for you, this one is conceived for you.

§143: You are born, O Horus, as the one whose name is He-before-Whom-the-Earth-Quakes; you are conceived, Seth, as the one whose name is He-before-Whom-the-Sky-Shakes. Such a one has no mutilation, such a one has no injury; so you have no injury, you have no mutilation.

§144: You are born for Osiris, O Horus! You have become more glorious than he, you have become more powerful than he.

§145: There is no seed of a god which has perished, neither has he who belongs to him. You will not perish, you who belongs to him. Re-Atum does not give you to Osiris, he does not reckon your heart, he has no power over your breast.

§146: Osiris, you cannot have power over him, your son cannot have power over him. Horus, you cannot have power over him, your father cannot have power over him.

§147: You belong, O this one, to this god, as the Twins of Atum said: "Lift yourself up," so said they, "in your name God," and so you become Atum for every god.

§148: Your head is that of Horus of the Duat, O Imperishable One; your brow is the One-with-the-Two-Eyes, O Imperishable One; your ears are the twins of Atum, O Imperishable One; your eyes are the twins of Atum, O Imperishable One; your nose is a jackal, O Imperishable One; your teeth are Sopdu, O Imperishable One.

§149: Your arms are Hapy and Dua-mutef, which you need to ascend to heaven, and you ascend; your legs are those of Imsety and Kebeh-senuf, which you need to descend to the lower sky, and you descend. All your members are the twins of Atum, O Imperishable One! You did not pass away, your Ka does not pass away. You are Ka!

pyramid_texts.title: Sarcophagus Chamber South Wall — Unas Encircled by the Duat
pyramid_texts.t:
§150: I have come to you, Nephthys, I have come to the Evening Barge, I have come to you, True-is-She-over-the-Red, I have come to you, She-Who-Remembers-the-Kas. Remember him, this Unas!

§151: Orion is encircled by the Duat, when the One-Who-Lives-in-the-Horizon purifies himself; Sothis is encircled by the Duat, when the One-Who-Lives-in-the-Horizon purifies himself. This Unas is encircled by the Duat, when the One-Who-Lives-in-the-Horizon purifies himself. He is content because of them, he is refreshed because of them, in the arms of his father, in the arms of Atum.

pyramid_texts.title: Sarcophagus Chamber South Wall — Announcement to the Four Directions
pyramid_texts.t:
§152: Re-Atum, Unas comes to you, an Imperishable Spirit, Lord of Dispensation in the site of the four papyrus columns. Your son comes to you, this Unas comes to you, that you both may stride over the sky, united in darkness, that you may rise on the horizon in the place where you like to be.

§153: Seth and Nephthys, hurry! Announce to the gods of the South and their spirits: He comes indeed, this Unas, an Imperishable Spirit! If he wills that you will die, you will die; if he wills that you will live, you will live.

§154: Re-Atum, Unas comes to you, an Imperishable Spirit, Lord of Dispensation in the site of the four papyrus columns. Your son comes to you, this Unas comes to you, that you both may stride over the sky, united in darkness, that you may rise on the horizon in the place where you like to be.

§155: Osiris and Isis, hurry! Announce to the gods of the North and their spirits: He comes indeed, this Unas, an Imperishable Spirit, like the Honored One over the Nile, so that the spirits in the waters honor him. Whom he wills that he live, he lives. Whom he wills that he die, he dies.

§156: Re-Atum, this Unas comes to you, an Imperishable Spirit, Lord of Dispensation in the site of the four papyrus columns. Your son comes to you, this Unas comes to you, that you both may stride over the sky, united in darkness, that you may rise on the horizon in the place where you like to be.

§157: Thoth, hurry! Announce to the gods of the West and their spirits: He comes indeed, this Unas, an Imperishable Spirit, decked like Anubis on the neck, who rules over the Western height, that he may reckon hearts and that he may have power over breasts! Whom he wills that he live, he lives. Whom he wills that he die, he dies.

§158: Re-Atum! Unas comes to you, an Imperishable Spirit, Lord of Dispensation in the site of the four papyrus columns. Your son comes to you, this Unas comes to you, that you both may stride over the sky, united in darkness, that you may rise on the horizon in the place where you like to be.

§159: Horus, hurry! Announce to the Eastern souls and to their spirits: He comes indeed, this Unas, an Imperishable Spirit! Whom he wills that he live, he lives. Whom he wills that he die, he dies.

§160: Re-Atum! Your son comes to you, Unas comes to you. Let him ascend to you! Enfold him in your embrace! This is the son of your body, eternally.

pyramid_texts.title: Sarcophagus Chamber South Wall — Unas Weary of the Nine
pyramid_texts.t:
§161: O Osiris, this Unas comes indeed, weary of the Nine, an Imperishable Spirit, to reckon hearts, to take Kas, to grant Kas. His every appointment obliges one to do his duty, him who he has elevated, and him who applied to him for it.

§162: There is no one who withdraws because he will have no more bread, his Ka will have no more bread, his bread will be withheld from him. Geb said, and it came forth from the mouth of the Ennead: "Hawk, after he has seized his own! Lo! you are ensouled and powerful!"

§163: He comes indeed, this Unas, weary of the Nine, an Imperishable Spirit — he that bore more than you, he that suffered more than you, he that is more weary than you, he that became greater than you, he who will be happier than you, he who roars louder than you. You have no more time there!

§164: Isis and Nephthys, come together, come together, unite! He comes indeed, this Unas, weary of the Nine, an Imperishable Spirit.

The Western Ones, those who are upon earth, belong to this Unas — He comes indeed, this Unas, weary of the Nine, an Imperishable Spirit.
The Eastern Ones, those who are upon earth, belong to this Unas — He comes indeed, this Unas, weary of the Nine, an Imperishable Spirit.
The Southern Ones, those who are upon earth, belong to this Unas — He comes indeed, this Unas, weary of the Nine, an Imperishable Spirit.
The Northern Ones, those who are upon earth, belong to this Unas — Those who are in the Lower Sky belong to this Unas — He comes indeed, this Unas, weary of the Nine, an Imperishable Spirit!

pyramid_texts.title: Sarcophagus Chamber South & East Walls — He Lives, He Judges
pyramid_texts.t:
§167: Atum, this your son is here, Osiris, whom you have preserved alive — he lives! He lives — this Unas lives! He is not dead, this Unas is not dead: he is not gone down, this Unas is not gone down: he has not been judged, this Unas has not been judged! He judges — this Unas judges!

§168: Shu, this your son is here, Osiris, whom you have preserved alive — he lives! He lives — this Unas lives! He is not dead, this Unas is not dead; he judges, this Unas judges!

§169: Tefnut, this your son is here, Osiris, whom you have preserved alive — he lives! He lives — this Unas lives! He judges, this Unas judges!

§170: Geb, this your son is here, Osiris, whom you have preserved alive — he lives! He lives — this Unas lives! He judges, this Unas judges!

§171: Nut, this your son is here, Osiris, whom you have preserved alive — he lives! He lives — this Unas lives! He judges, this Unas judges!

§172: Isis, this your brother is here, Osiris, whom you have preserved alive — he lives! He judges, this Unas judges!

§173: Seth, this your brother is here, Osiris, whom you have preserved alive, and who lives that he may punish thee — he lives — this Unas lives! He judges, this Unas judges!

§174: Nephthys, this your brother is here, Osiris, whom you have preserved alive — he lives! He judges, this Unas judges!

§175: Thoth, this your brother is here, Osiris, whom has been preserved alive, and who lives that he may punish you. He lives — this Unas lives! He judges, this Unas judges!

§176: Horus, this your father is here, Osiris, whom you have preserved alive — he lives! He judges, this Unas judges!

§177: Great Ennead, this Osiris is here, whom you have preserved alive — he lives! He judges, this Unas judges!

§178: Little Ennead, this Osiris is here, whom you have preserved alive — he lives! He judges, this Unas judges!

§179: Nunet, this your son Osiris is here, of whom you have said: "He is born for your father." You have wiped his mouth, his mouth has been opened by his son Horus, who is his beloved; his members have been reckoned by the gods.

§180–185: He lives — this Unas lives! He is not dead, this Unas is not dead: he is not gone down, this Unas is not gone down: he has not been judged, this Unas has not been judged. He judges, this Unas judges! In your name of He-in-Heliopolis-While-Enduring-Everlastingly-In-His-Necropolis — he lives, this Unas lives! In your name of He-in-Busiris, Chief of his Provinces — he lives! In your name of He-in-the-Castle-of-the-Scorpion, the appeased Ka — he lives! In your name of He-in-the-Divine-Hall, He-in-fumigation, He-in-the-Chest, He-in-the-Shrine — he lives! In your name He-in-the-White-Chapel-of-Paar-wood — he lives!

§186–192: In your name of He-in-Orion, your time is in heaven, your time is on earth. Osiris, turn your face so that you see this Unas, your seed which came out of you, the penetrating one! He lives — this Unas lives! He judges, this Unas judges! In your name of He-in-Buto; in your name He-in-the-Palace-of-the-Great-Oxen; in your name He-in-South-Hermopolis; in your name He-in-North-Hermopolis; in your name He-in-the-City-of-Lakes — what you have eaten is the Eye, your belly will be filled with it, your son Horus leaves it for you, that you may live by it.

§193: Your body is the body of this Unas, your flesh is the flesh of this Unas, your bones are the bones of this Unas. You go, this Unas goes: this Unas goes, you go.

pyramid_texts.title: Sarcophagus Chamber East Wall — The Great of Magic; Commands to the Land
pyramid_texts.t:
Utterance 220
§194: The doors of the horizon open themselves, its bolts slide. He has come to you, Net, crown of Lower Egypt; he has come to you, Nesert, Uraeus; he has come to you, Great One; he has come to you, Great of Magic, purified for you, in awe before you.

§195: Be pleased with him, be pleased with his purification, be pleased with the words he says to you: "How beautiful is your face when you are pleased, when you are new and young! A god has given you birth, the father of gods." He has come to you, O Great of Magic! It is Horus who fought to protect his eye, Great of Magic.

Utterance 221
§196–198: O Net, O Inu, O Great One! O Great of Magic, O Nesert! Inspire fear before Unas as fear before you, inspire dread before Unas as dread before you, inspire awe before Unas as awe before you, inspire love for Unas as love for you! Let him rule at the head of the living, let him be powerful at the head of the spirits, let his knife be firm against his enemies! O Inu, you came forth from him, he came forth from you. The Great Ikhet has given you birth, Ikhet-Utet has adorned you, for you are indeed Horus who fought to protect his eye.

Utterance 222
§199–213: Stand upon it, upon this land which came out of Atum, the spittle which came out of the Becoming One! May you become over it, may you be high over it, so that your father sees you, so that Re sees you! He comes to you, O his father; he comes to you, O Re; he comes to you, O Great Bull; he comes to you, O Sopdu, he comes to you, O Sharp-of-Teeth.

May you grant that this Unas seize the Cool Region and receive the horizon! May you grant that this Unas rule over the Nine, so that he provide the Ennead with gifts! May you give the herdman's staff into the hand of this Unas, so that the head of Lower and Upper Egypt be bowed in reverence!

You have adorned yourself as Great-of-Magic, He in Ombos, Lord of the South. Lo, you are full of glory, powerful one, more than the gods of the South, together with their spirits!

You go up and open the way through the bones of Shu; the embrace of your mother Nut enfolds you; you purify yourself on the horizon. You go up, you go down. You go down with Re, darkened with Nedy. You go up with Re and you rise with the Great Raft. You go up with Nephthys, darkened with the Evening Barge. You go up with Isis; you rise with the Morning Barge.

You have power over your body; there is no one to oppose you. You are born because of Horus in you, you are conceived because of Seth in you. You have come into being, you have become high, you have become a spirit! Cool it is for you in the embrace of your father, in the embrace of Atum.

Atum! Elevate to you this Unas, enfold him in your embrace! This is your son of your body, eternally.

pyramid_texts.title: Sarcophagus Chamber East Wall — The Offering Meal; Awakening
pyramid_texts.t:
Utterance 223
§214: To stir up, to turn around, O! O! O Unas, stand up, sit down to the thousand of bread, to the thousand of beer! The roast of your double rib is from the slaughter house, your Reteh-bread from the Wide Hall.

§215: As a god is supplied with the offering meal, Unas is supplied with this his bread. You have come to your soul, Osiris, who is mighty among the spirits, who is mighty in his places, who is under the protection of the Ennead in the Prince's Hall.

§216: O Unas, come up to me, betake you to me, do not be far from the tomb, your protection! I have given you the Eye of Horus, I have reckoned it to you. May it be pleasant for you!

§217: O Unas, stand up, receive this your bread from my hand! O Unas, I am your helper!

Utterance 224
§218–221: Awake, Unas! Turn around, Unas! You have gone to give orders to the places of Horus, you have gone to give orders to the places of Seth, you have gone to give orders to the places of Osiris.

May the king give the gift, in all your honors, in all your places! Your lotus-shaped scepter is at the head of the living, your staff is at the head of the spirits, like Anubis at the head of the Westerners, like Anedjty at the head of the Western nomes.

How pleasant is your condition! You become a spirit, O Unas, among your brothers the gods. How changed, how changed is your state! Therefore protect your children! Beware of your border which is on Earth! Put on your body and come towards them!
To say four times.

pyramid_texts.title: Sarcophagus Chamber East Wall Gable — Offering Liturgy; The Eye of Horus
pyramid_texts.t:
Utterance 204
§118: Let the hoers be in jubilation, the heart of Thesesu-breast be exalted! They have swallowed the Eye of Horus, the healthy one, the one in Heliopolis. The finger of Unas, the small one, draws out that which is in the navel of Osiris.

§119: Unas is not thirsty, he is not hungry, the heart of Unas is not faint, for the arms of the Desert God keep away his hunger! Fill! Make the hearts full!

Utterance 205
§120: O you who preside over the offerings, O you who belong to Plenty, Unas has been directed to Fetek, the cupbearer of Re! Re has directed him himself. Re sends him to the overseers of provender of this year: what they seize, they give it to him; they give him barley and spelt, bread and beer.

§121: For it is to Unas that his father granted, that Re granted, barley and spelt, bread and beer. For it is he, the Great Bull who strikes Nubia; to Unas belong the five portions of bread, drink and cakes in the Hall, three of which are in the sky with Re, two are on earth with the two Enneads.

§122: For he is the unbound one being unbound, for he is the seen one being seen. Says Re: "It is better for him today than yesterday."

§123: Unas has united himself to the Moist, he kissed the Dry Seat, Unas joined himself to the flame, Unas unites himself to the Beautiful One. It is the Beautiful One who fears Unas, and she gives bread to Unas: she does him good on this day.

Utterance 207
§124: Offering of the butcher, offering of that which is in the Eye of Re! Offering of the birdcatcher, of that which is in the eye of the god, the cupbearer who brings water! Let the flame burn! The joint together with the pastry! Four hands full of water.

Utterance 209
§125: Shu is flourishing. Unas has not taken away his meal! Unas is flourishing. Shu has not taken away his meal! The messengers of the East repeat: "This is your bread!"

Utterance 210
§126–130: Judge, arise! Thoth, be high; sleepers wake, the inhabitants of Nubia arise, before the Great Trembler who comes out of the nome, before the Opener-of-the-Way who comes out of the bush!

Pure is the mouth of Unas! The two Enneads cense Unas. Pure indeed is the tongue which is in his mouth! Excrement is an abomination to Unas. Unas rejects urine, Unas loathes his abomination.

May Unas eat of what you eat, drink of what you drink, live on what you live, sit on what you sit, be strong in what you are strong, sail in what you sail!

The pavilion of Unas is woven in the Field of Rushes, the plenty of Unas is in the Field of Offerings. His offering is among you, you gods! The water of Unas is wine, like that of Re; Unas goes round about the sky like Re, he traverses the sky like Thoth.

Utterance 211
§131–132: The abomination of Unas is hunger, he does not eat it; the abomination of Unas is thirst, he does not drink it. Unas it is, indeed, who gives bread to the Existing Ones; his nurse is the milk-goddess. It is she who makes him live again, it is she who gives Unas birth. Unas is conceived at night, Unas is born at night, for he belongs to the Followers of Re who are before the Morning Star. Unas is conceived in the Watery Abyss, he is being born in the Watery Abyss. He has come, he has brought your bread which he has found there!

Utterance 212
§133: The Eye of Horus trickles on the bush of the djenu-plant. The-One-at-the-Head-of-the-Westerners comes to him indeed, he has brought him the food of Horus-Who-Is-at-the-Head-of-His-Houses. On what he lives, Unas lives on it; of what he eats, Unas eats; of what he drinks, Unas drinks. One joint and one cake — this is his offering.

pyramid_texts.title: Sarcophagus Chamber West Wall Gable — Serpent Spells
pyramid_texts.t:
Utterance 226
§225: A serpent is entwined by a serpent, when a young hippopotamus coming on the pasture is entwined. Earth, swallow that which came out of you! Monster, lie down, glide away!
§226: The majesty of the pelican falls in water. Serpent, turn over that Re may see you!

Utterance 227
§227: The head of the great black bull is cut off. Hepenu-serpent, this I say to you, Kheser-neter-scorpion, this I say to you: "Turn over, glide into the ground!" I have said this to you.

Utterance 228
§228: A face falls on a face, a face has seen a face. The mottled knife, black and green, went forth against it: it has swallowed that which it tasted.

Utterance 229
§229: This is the nail of Atum upon the dorsal vertebrae of the Neheb-Kau-serpent, which stopped the strife in Wenu. Fall! Glide away!

Utterance 230
§230–234: Let your two poison glands be in the ground! Let your two rows of ribs be in the hole! Pour out the liquid! The Two Kites stand by. Your mouth is closed by the follower's tool; the mouth of the follower's tool is closed by the lynx.

O Re, Unas has bitten the earth, Unas has bitten Geb, Unas has bitten the father of he who bit him. This is the being who has bitten Unas; Unas did not bite him. It is he who comes against Unas; Unas does not go against him. If you bite Unas, he will make you one; if you look on Unas he will make you two.

The male serpent is bitten by the female serpent, the female serpent is bitten by the male serpent. Heaven is enchanted, earth is enchanted, the Male behind mankind is enchanted. Enchanted will be the god Blind-is-his-head. You, yourself, scorpion, will be enchanted. These are the two knots of Elephantine which are in the mouth of Osiris, knotted for Horus over the backbone.

Utterances 231–243 (Further Serpent Spells)
§235–248: Your bone is made into a harpoon by which you will be harpooned. Hearts are removed; the nomads are in the place of the spear, they are overthrown.

A face is upon you, you who are on your bowels. Fall on your backbone! Retreat before me, serpent provided with his two faces!

The serpent which came forth from Earth is fallen, the flame which came from the Watery Abyss is fallen. Fall! Glide away!

The Uraeus serpent is for the sky; the centipede of Horus is for the earth. Horus, an oxherd, treads; Unas has trod upon the walk of Horus. A face is upon you, you who are in his naut-bush. Meat for the pot of Horus, escape into the earth! O let the beast, O desert, glide away!

Extinguished is the flame! The flame-serpent is not to be found in the house of he who possesses Ombos. It is a serpent which will bite, which has slipped into the house of him whom it will bite, that it may remain in it.

Two hetes-scepters and two hetes-scepters for two djema-ropes! As bread! Interlace then! You should be here indeed. Servant! Take away!

pyramid_texts.title: Sarcophagus Chamber North Wall, First Register — Purification; Offering Rites; Eye of Horus
pyramid_texts.t:
Utterance 23
§16: Osiris, seize every one who hates Unas, who speaks evil against his name! Thoth, go, seize him for Osiris! Bring the one who speaks evil against the name of Unas, place him in your hand! To say four times: Do not separate yourself from him, take care that you not be separated from him.

Utterance 25
§17–18: He goes who goes with his Ka. Horus goes with his Ka, Seth goes with his Ka, Thoth goes with his Ka, the God goes with his Ka, He-With-Two-Eyes goes with his Ka. You also go with your Ka. O Unas, the arm of your Ka is before you; O Unas, the arm of your Ka is behind you; O Unas, the leg of your Ka is before you; O Unas, the leg of your Ka is behind you! Osiris Unas, I give you the Eye of Horus, that your face may be adorned with it, that the perfume of the Eye of Horus may spread towards you!

Utterance 32
§22–23: This is your libation, Osiris, this is your libation, O Unas, coming from your son, coming from Horus. I have come, I bring you the Eye of Horus, so that your heart may be refreshed by it. I bring it to you to carry you, to be under your soles. Take the efflux which comes out of you, that your heart may not be weary thereby. To say four times: Take! The voice has come out for you.

Utterances 34–42 (Purification Rites)
§26–32: Semin, semin, open your mouth, O Unas! You taste its taste in front of the divine chapels, that which Horus spits out, semin, that which Seth spits out, semin, the two Harmonious Ones, semin. To say four times: You purify yourself with natron, together with the Followers of Horus.

You purify yourself, Horus purifies himself; you purify yourself, Seth purifies himself; you purify yourself, Thoth purifies himself; the god purifies himself; you make yourself pure with what is amongst them, so that your mouth is the mouth of a milk calf on the day of its birth.

You purify yourself, your Ka purifies himself; this your own self purifies you among your brothers the gods. You purify your mouth, you make pure all your bones; you are adorned with what is yours. O Osiris, I give you the Eye of Horus that you may adorn your face with it.

O Unas, I make firm for you your two separated jaws. I open for you your mouth! Unas, take the Eye of Horus to which he went! I bring it to you, put it into your mouth. Take the tip of the bodily breast of Horus, take it into your mouth! Take the full breast of your sister Isis, bring it unto your mouth!

Utterances 43–57 (Offering Presentations)
§33–40: Take the two Eyes of Horus, the black and the white one, seize them for your front, that they may brighten your face! May Re in heaven be pleased with you, may he appease for you the Two Lords. Osiris Unas, take the white teeth of Horus which equip your mouth! A boon-the-king-gives for the Ka of Unas.

Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus snatched from Seth, which you shall take to your mouth, that you open your mouth with it! Osiris Unas, take the liquid which came out of you! Unas, take the Eye of Horus that you may taste it!

Unas, take the Eye of Horus which was snatched from Seth, which was rescued for you, that you may open your mouth with it! Unas, take the Eye of Horus which was rescued for you, which will not separate itself from you! Unas, take the Eye of Horus that you may be provided with it!

pyramid_texts.title: Sarcophagus Chamber North Wall, Second Register — Anointing; Linen; Bread and Beer
pyramid_texts.t:
Utterances 72–79 (Anointing with Sacred Oils)
§50–54: Osiris Unas, I make full your eye for you with ointment. Osiris Unas, take the outflow of his face — Hekenu-oil. Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus on account of which he fought — Sefeth-oil. Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus of which he took possession — Neshenem-oil. Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus which brought the gods to him through it — Tuat-oil.

O ointment, O ointment, arise, hurry! You who are on the brow of Horus, arise! You are placed on the brow of this Unas, so that he may feel sweet under you, that you make him a spirit under you. You grant him to have power over his body; you grant that his terror be in the eyes of all the spirits when they look at him, and of everyone who hears his name.

Osiris Unas, I bring you the Eye of Horus which he takes, which is on your brow — First quality Libyan oil. Osiris Unas, the sound Eye of Horus is being rubbed on your face — Two pouches of green eye cosmetic.

Utterance 81
§56–57: You awake in peace, the goddess Tayt awakes in peace, Taytyt awakes in peace! The Eye of Horus in Dep is in peace, the Eye of Horus in the Mansions of the Northern Crown is in peace. Cause the Two Lands to bow before this Unas as they bow before Horus! Cause the Two Lands to fear Unas as they fear Seth! Be seated before Unas as his god, open his way in front of the spirits, that he may stand in front of the spirits like Anubis, He-at-the-Head-of-the-Westerners! Forward, forward, before Osiris!

Utterances 82–96 (Further Offering Presentations)
§58–64: It is Thoth who came with it, he has come out carrying the Eye of Horus. Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus after he has been satisfied with it! Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus, join it to your mouth!

Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus, the diminished one, of which Seth has eaten! Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus which they, acting against him, destroyed!

Lift up your face, Osiris; lift up your face, O Unas, he whose spirit goes. Lift up your face, Unas, honored and sharp, that you see what comes out of you! Wash yourself, Unas, open your mouth with the Eye of Horus! Call your Ka, like Osiris, that he may protect you against every kind of wrath of the dead! Unas, receive this your bread which is the Eye of Horus!

Utterances 108–116
§72–74: Osiris Unas, unite to yourself the water which is in it! Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus which purifies his mouth with natron. Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus, unite it to your mouth! Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus, the trampled by Seth! Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus pulled out by him! Osiris Unas, I bring you what causes you joy. Osiris Unas, I place your Eye, the tasty. Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus! Prevent him from suffering because of it!

pyramid_texts.title: Sarcophagus Chamber North Wall, Third Register — The Great Offering List
pyramid_texts.t:
§75–100: The great offering liturgy of the Eye of Horus — bread, beer, meat, fowl, fruit, grain, and wine — each gift an aspect of the sacred Eye, restored to Osiris-Unas.

Utterance 117: Osiris Unas, receive your head! — Four shenes-loaves.
Utterance 118: Osiris Unas, take your Eye, seize it! — Four imta-loaves.
Utterance 119: Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus, which he swallowed — Four cake baskets.
Utterance 120: Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus in its glory — Four hebenenet-baskets.
Utterance 121: Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus, pulled out by him — Four kemeh-loaves.
Utterance 122: Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus, which is placed in the mouth for you — Four idat-cakes.
Utterance 123: Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus, your cake, that you may eat — Four pat-cakes.
Utterance 124: Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus, which he pulled out — Four pieces of roast.
Utterance 125: Osiris Unas, bring to yourself these white and healthy teeth — Four bunches of onions.
Utterance 126: Osiris Unas, take khepekh, the Eye of Horus — One foreleg.
Utterance 127: Osiris Unas, dance! Geb did not sin against his heir who inherited — One joint of meat.
Utterances 128–131: Osiris Unas, take what replaces the Eye of Horus; take those who rebel against you; take your assailant; take the Eye of Horus — may you go towards it — One liver; one spleen.
Utterances 132–141: Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus which is on his brow; on the brow of Seth; take the severed heads of the Followers of Seth — One ra-goose; one therep-goose; one set-goose; one sr-goose; one pigeon; one tasif-bread.
Utterances 142–171: Osiris Unas, take the Eye of Horus — it shall not be cut off from you! The Eye of Horus is reckoned for you. Take the water; the diminished Eye of which Seth has eaten; the Eye they destroyed. Equip yourself with the liquid which comes out of you — beer, wine of the North, wine of Buto, wine of Pelusium; figs, wheat and aghet-corn, bebat-grain, nebes fruit, sweet fruit, fresh vegetables.

Utterance 171: Osiris Unas, hey! Existence is for you, and with you, with you! — Offering.

pyramid_texts.title: Passage Walls — Libation; Incense; Unas Ascends as a Hawk
pyramid_texts.t:
Passage North Wall — Utterances 199, 32, 23, 25, 200

Utterance 199
§115: O Osiris Unas, turn towards this your bread! Receive it from my hand! May the Eye of Horus flourish for you! Divine offering: bread, cake, and liquid.

Utterance 200
§116: Salutation, incense! Salutation, brother divine! Salutation, Men-wer, he who is in the flesh of Horus! Great father, spread out in your name "Pellet"! Your smell is for Unas, your perfume is for Unas! Eye of Horus, be high, be great for Unas! — Incense.

Passage South Wall — Utterances 244–246

Utterance 244
§249: This is here the hard Eye of Horus. Place it in your hand that you may be sure of victory and that he — Seth — may fear you! Breaking of two red jars.

Utterance 245
§250–251: This Unas comes to you, O Nut, this Unas comes to you, O Nut. He has thrown his father down to earth, he has left a Horus behind him. His two wings have grown as those of a hawk, his two feathers are those of a holy hawk. His soul has brought him here, his magical power has adorned him.

May you open your place in heaven amongst the stars of heaven! You are indeed the unique star, the comrade of Hu. May you look down on Osiris, when he gives orders to the spirits! You stand high up, far from him. You are not of them, you shall not be of them.

Utterance 246
§252–256: See! This Unas stands among you, two horns are on his head like two wild bulls, for you are indeed the black ram, son of a black sheep, born of a bright sheep, suckled by four sheep-mothers.

He comes against you, Horus with blue eyes. Beware of the Horus with red eyes, whose anger is evil, whose power one cannot withstand! His messengers go, his quick runners run. The gods are silent before you, the Ennead has put their hands before their mouths.

Step to the doors of the horizon, and the doors of the Cool Region open themselves. You stand there as a king, ruling over them as Geb rules over his Ennead.

They see you as Min, who rules over the two shrines. He stands, who stands behind you; your brother stands behind you; your relative stands behind you; you do not go under, you will not be annihilated, your name remains with men, your name comes into being with the gods.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber West Wall Gable — Unas Enthroned; The Lotus at the Nose of Re
pyramid_texts.t:
Utterance 247
§257–261: Your son Horus has done this for you. The great ones tremble when they have seen the sword which is in your hand, when you come out of the dusk. Hail to you, Wise One! Geb has created you, the Ennead has given you birth. Horus is satisfied with his father, Atum is satisfied with his years.

Unas there, O Unas, see! Unas there, O Unas, look! Unas there, O Unas, hear! Unas there, O Unas, be there! Unas there, O Unas, arise on your side! Do as I order, you who hate sleep, you who are tired! Get up, you who are in Nedjit! Your fine bread is made here in Buto. Receive your power in Heliopolis!

It is Horus to whom order was given to do this for his father. To the Lord of the Storm, wrath is forbidden when he carries you. It is he who will carry Atum, the All.

Utterance 248
§262–263: Unas is a great one, Unas came out between the thighs of the divine Ennead. Unas was conceived by Sekhmet; it is Shesmet who gave him birth as a star with sharp front sight, with wide stride, which brings provender for the road of Re every day. Unas has come to his throne which is over the Two Goddesses who protect Upper and Lower Egypt, and Unas appears as a star.

Utterance 249
§264–266: Unas is from that sesh-sesh-plant which came out of earth; his hand is cleansed by the one who prepared his seat. Unas is this flower at the nose of the Great Mighty One. Unas has come out of the Isle of Fire, after he has placed truth there in the place of falsehood. Unas is the guardian of washing, who watches over the Uraei on that night of the Great Flood which comes out of the Great One.

Unas appears as Nefertem, the lotus flower at the nose of Re, as he comes out of the Horizon every day, and at the sight of whom the gods purify themselves.

Utterance 250
§267–268: Unas is he who is over the Kas, who unites hearts from the One-over-Wisdom, he is the Great One who is in possession of the Divine Book, the Wisdom at the right of Re. Unas comes to his seat, which is over the Kas; Unas unites the hearts; Unas has become Wisdom, in possession of the Divine Book at the right of Re. Unas says what is in the heart of She-the-Great-One on the Feast of Red Cloth. He is the ruler of the cavern of Nun.

Utterances 251–253
§269–275: O you who are set over the hours, you who go in front of Re, prepare a way for Unas! Unas is on the way to his throne which is in front of other seats behind the god. Unas has overpowered those who were to be punished, Unas has smashed their fronts. The arm of Unas will not be opposed in the horizon.

Lift up your face, you gods who are in the Duat! Unas has come, that you might see him, having become a Great God. Lead Unas with trembling, attire Unas. Unas is powerful. Unas lifts his ames-scepter. Unas sits together with the rowers of the barge of Re. Unas orders the good, and he executes it. Unas is the Great God.

He is purified, who has purified himself in the Fields of Rushes; Re has purified himself in the Fields of Rushes. This Unas has purified himself in the Fields of Rushes. The hand of Unas is in the hand of Re. Nut, take his hand! Shu, lift him up! Shu, lift him up!

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber West Wall — The Cannibal Hymn; Unas Lord of Heaven
pyramid_texts.t:
Utterance 254
§276–294: The Great One fumigates the Bull of Nehen, the heat of the fiery breath is against you who are about the shrine of the sun god. O Great God whose name is unknown, bring at once a meal of the Unique Lord. O lord of the Horizon, make place for Unas! If you fail to make place for Unas, Unas will pronounce a curse against his father Geb: the earth shall not speak any more, Geb shall not be able to defend himself.

He whom Unas finds on his way, he will eat him piecemeal.

See, she comes to meet you, the Beautiful West, to meet you with her beautiful locks! She says: "He comes whom I have borne, whose horn shines, the well anointed pillar, the Bull of Heaven. Your form is exalted, pass by in peace!" "I have preserved you," so says she, the Beautiful West, to Unas.

Unas is the Unique One, the Bull of Heaven. He has exterminated those who did this against him, he has annihilated their offspring upon earth.

Utterance 255
§295–300: The horizon fumigates before Horus of Nehen — a meal for the Lords. O Ugly One, whose essence is ugly, whose form is ugly — go away from your seat, lay down on the ground your dignity for Unas. If you do not go from your seat and lay down on the ground your dignity for this Unas, Unas will come with a face like this Great One, the Lord of the lion helmet, who became powerful through the injury of his eye.

The Great One rises then in his shrine. He lays down his dignity on the ground for Unas after he has seized Hu and taken possession of Sia.

Utterance 256
§301–303: Unas has inherited Geb, Unas has inherited Geb! He has inherited Atum, he is on the throne of Horus the eldest! His Eye is in his strength, his protection is what has been done against him. Unas has put his fear into their hearts by making a massacre amongst them. The gods have seen it, while they took their clothes off; they bow before Unas while praising: "Row him, O his mother, tow him, O native place! Hey, loose the rope!"

Utterances 257–260
§304–323: Excitement in heaven! "We see something new!" say the gods of Primeval Times. "O Ennead, a new Horus is in the sunlight, the lords of forms serve him, the Two whole Enneads attend him, as he sits on the seat of the Lord of All. Unas takes heaven, he splits its brass, Unas is led on the ways of the Becoming One."

"Unas goes to peace, being alive in the West, and the inhabitants of the Duat serve him. Unas shines again in the East, the One-Who-Separates-the-Quarrelers comes to him, bowing. Serve him, you gods, he is older than the Great One."

Unas takes Hu, Eternity is brought to him, Sia is placed at his feet. Jubilate for Unas, he has taken the Horizon!

Osiris is Unas in a dust storm. His horror is the earth. Unas did not enter into Geb that he might be annihilated, that he might sleep in his house upon earth, that his bones might be broken. He has purified himself with the Eye of Horus. Unas is on the way to heaven, Unas is on the way to heaven, with the wind, with the wind. He will not be hindered, there is no one who might hinder him.

O Geb, Bull of Nut, a Horus is Unas, the heir of his father. Unas is he who went and came back. The Two Truths judged, while Shu was a witness. The Two Truths have decreed that the thrones of Geb should come to him. Unas comes out on this day in the true form of a living spirit. Unas comes out, the guardian of Truth, he brings it while it is with him.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber South Wall — Heart-Thrower; The Reed Floats; The Great Ferryboat
pyramid_texts.t:
Utterance 261
§324–325: Unas is a heart-thrower, the son of the heart of Shu. He is spread out an outspreading, with a terrible light. Unas it is who burns before the wind to the limits of heaven, to the limits of earth, as soon as the hands of Lightning are emptied of Unas. Unas traverses the air and passes over the earth. He kisses the Red Crown as one hurled by a god. Those in the tree crowns open their arms to him. Unas stands on the east side of the vault of Heaven. It is Unas, the message of the Storm.

Utterance 262
§327–336: Ignore not Unas, O god! You know him for he knows you. Ignore not Unas, O Re! It is to be said to you — "Greatest One of all the annihilated." Ignore not Unas, O Thoth — "The one in peace." Ignore not Unas, O Horus Sothis — "Unfortunate One." Ignore not Unas, O You who are in the Duat — "He who awakes in good health." Ignore not Unas, O Bull of Heaven — "This Neheh-star."

See, Unas comes! See, Unas comes! See, Unas has gone up! Unas, however, comes not by himself; it is an embassy which came to him. Unas has passed by his dangerous place, the fury of the great sea avoided him. Unas has reached the height of Heaven! He has seen his Self in the Night Barge; it is Unas who rowed on it. He has recognized his Swelling Uraeus in the Morning Barge. It was Unas who bailed it out. The People of Light bore witness for him; they let Unas ascend to Re.

Utterance 263
§337–341: The two Reed Floats of the sky are laid down for Re, that he may cross to the Horizon. The two Reed Floats of the sky are laid down for Horus of the Horizon. The two reed floats of the sky are laid down for Unas, that he may cross on them to Horus of the Horizon, to Re.

It was pleasant for Unas to be with his Ka and he lives together with his Ka. His panther skirt is on him, his Ames-scepter is on his arm, his Aba-scepter is in his hand. The Fields of Rushes are filled with water to let Unas cross the Sinuous Watercourse. This Unas will cross a crossing to the eastern side of the Horizon. His sister is Sothis, his place of birth is the Twilight, the Duat.

Utterances 267–272 (Selected)
§364–392: Your heart belongs to you, O Osiris; your two feet belong to you, O Osiris; your arm belongs to you, O Osiris. The heart of Unas belongs to him, himself; his two feet belong to him; his arm belongs to him.

The earth is beaten into steps for him towards heaven, that he may mount on it towards heaven, and he rises on the smoke of the great fumigation. He flies away, this Unas, as goose; he alights as a beetle; he flies away as a goose; he alights as a beetle on the empty throne which is in your boat, O Re.

Stand up, begone, you who do not know the thicket of rushes, that Unas may sit on your seat, that he may row in the sky in your boat, O Re! This Unas pushes off from Earth being in your boat, O Re. When you come out of the Horizon, he has his scepter in his hand.

This Unas washes himself, Re appears, the great Ennead shines. This Unas ravishes mankind as his own limb; this Unas seizes the Very Great Crown from the two Enneads. Isis takes care of him, Nephthys suckles him. Horus takes him to his side, purifies this Unas in the Jackal Lake, cleans the Ka of this Unas in the Lake of Dawn.

Awake in peace, You-Whose-Face-is-Behind, in peace, Ferryman of the Sky, in peace, Ferryman of Nut, in peace, Ferryman of the Gods! Unas comes to you, that you may ferry him in that ferryboat in which you ferry the gods. There is no accuser about a living one against Unas, there is no accuser about a dead one against Unas.

If you do not ferry Unas, he will jump up and place himself on the wing of Thoth. It is he who will then ferry him over to this other side.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall Gable — The Cannibal Hymn of Unas
pyramid_texts.t:
§393–414: The sky is clouded, the stars are darkened. The Bows move, the bones of the Earth God tremble. Then all movements cease after they have seen Unas appearing and powerful as a god, who lives on his fathers, who feeds on his mothers.

Unas is a lord of craft, whose name his mother does not know. Unas' honor is in the sky, his power is in the horizon, like his father Atum who begat him more powerful than himself.

The Kas of Unas are behind him, his maidservants are under his feet, his gods are over him, his Uraei are on his brow. The might of Unas is for his protection.

Unas is the Bull of Heaven, who once suffered want and who has decided to live on the essence of every god, who eats their entrails when they come from the Isle of Fire with their bellies full of magical charms.

Unas is a well provided one, who has absorbed his spirits. Unas has appeared as this Great One, lord of those who are at hand. He sits with his back turned to Geb.

Unas it is who judges with He-whose-Name-is-Hidden, on the day when the elder one is being sacrificed. Unas is the lord of offerings, who knots the cord, who prepares himself his meal.

Unas is he who eats men, who lives on gods, lord of messengers who gives instructions.

Indeed, He-Who-Seizes-by-the-Hair is he who lassoes them for Unas. Indeed, the snake Lifted-Head is he who keeps guard over them for him. Indeed, Khonsu, who slaughters the lords, cuts their throats for Unas and takes out for him what is in their bellies — Khonsu is the messenger who he sends out to chastise. Wine Press God cuts them up for Unas and cooks for him a meal out of them in his evening cooking pots.

Their great ones are for his morning meal, their middle-sized ones for his evening meal, their little ones for his night meal, their old men and the old women are for his fuel. The Great Ones in the Northern Sky light fire for him under the kettles which contain them.

Unas is the great Power, who has power over the Powers. Unas is the Akhem-hawk, the hawk of hawks, the great one. He whom he finds on his way, he eats him bit by bit.

Unas is a god older than the eldest. Thousands serve him, hundreds make offerings to him. A certificate is given him as a Great Power by Orion, the father of the gods.

Unas has appeared again in heaven. He is crowned with the Upper Egyptian crown as Lord of the Horizon. He has reckoned up the dorsal vertebrae, he has seized the hearts of the gods.

He has eaten the Red One, the crown; he has swallowed the Green One. Unas feeds on the lungs of the wise. His pleasure is to live on hearts, as well as on their magic.

Unas' span of life is Eternity, his limit is Everlastingness in this his dignity of "If-he-Wishes-He-Does, If-He-Wishes-Not-He-Does-Not," he is in the region of the Horizon eternally to eternity.

Lo, their soul is in the belly of Unas, their spirits are with Unas as the broth of the gods, cooked for Unas from their bones.

Unas is that which appears, which appears, which remains, which remains. The doers of evil shall not be able to destroy the favorite seat of Unas amongst the living in this land, eternally to eternity.

Utterance 275–276
§415–417: Unas comes to you, you hawks, although your houses are closed for Unas. His loincloth is on his back, made of the hide of a baboon. Unas opens the gate with the double doors, Unas reaches the limit of the Horizon. Unas will become a Great One who resides in Crocodilopolis.

Your deed be against you, what you will do will be against you, O Seksek-serpent, he who is in his hole, O adversary!

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber North Wall — Unas Flies to Heaven; The Ladder
pyramid_texts.t:
Utterance 302
§458–463: The sky is serene, Sothis lives, for it is Unas indeed who is the living star, the son of Sothis. The two Enneads have purified themselves for him as the Great Bear constellation which cannot perish. The house of Unas which is in the sky will not perish, the throne of Unas which is on earth will not be destroyed.

Men hide themselves, the gods fly up, Sothis has let Unas fly towards Heaven amongst his brothers, the gods. Nut, the Great, has uncovered her arms for Unas. The two souls at the head of the souls of Heliopolis have bowed down at the beginning of the day. The throne of Unas is with you, O Re; he will not give it to any other god.

He ascends towards heaven to you, O Re, while his face is like that of hawks, his wings are like those of geese, his talons like the fangs of the god of the Djuf Nome.

There is no word against Unas on earth among men. There is no crime of Unas in the sky among gods. Unas has done away with the word against him, Unas has annulled it, in order to rise towards heaven. Unas has moved his arms like a semen-goose, he has beaten with his wings like a kite. He flies up, he who flies up, O men. Unas also flies up away from you.

Utterance 303
§464–467: You Gods of the West, you Gods of the East, you Gods of the South, you Gods of the North! These four pure reed floats which you placed for Osiris when he ascended towards heaven — place them for Unas. Are you Horus, son of Osiris? Are you, O Unas, the god, the eldest one, the son of Hathor? Are you the seed of Geb? Osiris has ordered that Unas may appear as a second Horus.

Utterance 304
§468–471: Hail to you, daughter of Anubis, she who stands at the windows of the sky, you friend of Thoth, she who stands at the two side rails of the ladder! Open the way for Unas that he may pass. Hail, O ostrich standing on the shore of the winding stream! Open the way for Unas. Hail to you, Bull of Re, you with the four horns — your one horn is in the West, your one horn is in the East, your one horn is in the South, your one horn is in the North! Bow that Western horn of yours for Unas, that Unas may pass.

Utterance 305
§472–475: The ladder is tied together by Re before Osiris. The ladder is tied together by Horus before his father Osiris, when he goes to his spirit. One of them is on this side, one of them is on that side, while Unas is between them. "Are you then a god whose places are pure?" "I come from a pure place." "Stand here, O Unas," says Horus. "Sit here, Unas," says Seth. "Take this arm," says Re. The spirit belongs to heaven, the body to the earth.

Utterances 306–312
§476–501: How beautiful is indeed the sight, how good indeed to see! So say the gods, when this god ascends to heaven, when Unas ascends to heaven, while his power is over him, the fear on both his sides; his magical power in front of his legs.

They come towards him, the Divine Souls of Buto, the Divine Souls of Hierakonpolis, the gods of the sky, the gods of the earth. They elevate Unas on their arms. And you ascend, Unas, to heaven — "Heaven be given to Unas, earth be given to him!" So said Atum.

A native of Heliopolis is in Unas, O God. Unas himself is from Heliopolis, born in Heliopolis when Re ruled the Two Enneads. He is the heir of his father Geb.

Hail to you, O Horus in the Horite sites, hail to you, O Seth in the Sethan sites, hail to you, Reed God in the Fields of Rushes! Unas saw you as Horus saw Isis; Unas saw you as Neheb-kau saw the Scorpion Goddess; Unas saw you as Sobek saw Neith; Unas saw you as Seth saw the Two Harmonious Ones.

Unas is the thrasher of gods. Unas sits before him, he opens his chests, unseals his decrees, seals his book rolls; Unas sends his messengers who do not tire.

See Unas, O Re, recognize Unas, O Re! He is one of them who know you. May She-Who-Locks-Out-When-She-Locks-Out open the doors of the Horizon for the coming out of the Morning Barge. O you, His-Face-in-Front-His-Face-Behind, bring this to Unas — the one which flies up, which alights.

May the bread fly up, may the bread continue to fly up to my houses, to the houses of the Crown of Lower Egypt!

pyramid_texts.title: Corridor Walls — Unas as Sobek; The Seven Enneads; Lord of the Night
pyramid_texts.t:
Corridor West Wall — Utterances 313–317

Utterance 313
§502–503: The phallus of Babay is pulled out, the doors of the sky are open. The doors of the sky are locked, the way leads over the fire glow, under that which assembles the gods. What lets every Horus glide through will also let Unas glide through. Unas is a Horus.

Utterance 314
§504: Back, you ox who should be slaughtered, in whose horns should be the fingers of Aker! Fall, glide away!

Utterance 315
§505: Unas is a Ian-baboon, a Hetet-baboon, a Patet-baboon. Unas' bottom is according to Unas' own wish; blessedness is on the head of Unas. Unas will make the jubilations of those who jubilate. He will sit among you, youthful ones.

Utterance 316
§506: O Hemy and Sehed, Unas does not give you his magical power. Unas will sit, his back towards She, the Holy One in Heliopolis. Take Unas to the sky!

Utterance 317
§507–510: Unas came today, out of the overflow of the flood. Unas is Sobek, with green feather, with a watchful face, with uplifted brow, rushing up, coming from the leg and the tail of the Great One, she who resides in the brilliant light.

Unas came to his water currents, which are in the land of the flood of the Great Overflow, the sky, to the place of peace with green pastures on the horizon. Unas causes the grass to become green on the two banks of the horizon. Unas brings the green brilliance to the Great Eye which resides among the pastures. Unas takes his seat which is on the horizon.

Unas arises as Sobek, the son of Neith. Unas eats with his mouth, Unas urinates, Unas copulates with his phallus. Unas is the lord of seed, he who takes the women from their husbands, wherever Unas wants, according to the desire of his heart.

Corridor East Wall — Utterances 318–321

Utterance 318
§511–512: Unas is the Nau-snake, the leading bull, who has swallowed his seven Uraei, and so his seven neck vertebrae came into being; he who gives orders to his seven Enneads who hear the word of the king.

Unas has come, he swallows myrrh. Unas takes myrrh, he wallows in myrrh, the nails of Unas are full of myrrh. Unas has taken your necks, O gods. Serve Unas so that he invests you with your Kas.

Utterance 319
§513–514: Unas is the bull of double brilliance in the midst of his Eye. Safe is the mouth of Unas through the fiery breath; the head of Unas through the horns of the Lord of the South. Unas leads the god. Unas rules over the Ennead. Unas lets the lapis lazuli grow. Unas has twisted the shem-shem-plant into ropes. Unas has united the heavens. Unas rules over the lands, the South and the North, as the god of those who were before. Unas has built a divine city as it should be. Unas is the third when he appears.

Utterance 320
§515–516: Unas has regulated the night, Unas has sent the stars on their way. The Powers appear; they honor Unas with the title of Babay. Unas is the son of her who did not know that she gave birth to Unas, for Powerful Face, the Lord of Nights. Humble yourselves, you lords; hide yourselves, you subjects, before Unas. Unas is Babay, the Lord of the Night, the Bull of Apes, who lives without knowing it.

Utterance 321
§517: O you, Whose Back Is on His Back, bring to Unas the seferet of the offering-meal which is on the back of Osiris, so that Unas may ascend on it to heaven, so that Unas may serve Re as courtier in the sky.
